outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms will be possible from the central Plains to the upper Midwest Saturday afternoon and evening. Isolated to widely scattered severe storms will also be possible across parts of Upstate New York and northern New England.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: A mid-level ridge will build farther eastward today, with anticyclonic flow amplifying over much of the East Coast. Farther west, a broad trough will gradually overspread the Missouri and upper Mississippi Valleys, with a belt of enhanced southwesterly flow persisting from the central Rockies to the upper Great Lakes. Within this flow regime, a series of convectively augmented impulses will lift northeast from the southern/central High Plains to Ontario, offering multiple zones of convective focus through the period.

sections.title: Plains to the Midwest
sections.text: A fairly complex evolution is expected today, owing to the placement of outflow boundaries from overnight convection and the subsequent position of the effective front. Most likely, this boundary will be situated from parts of western Kansas northeastward to Minnesota by the afternoon. To its east (generally from eastern Kansas to the upper Midwest), dew points in the 70s will combine with pockets of insolation (influenced by convective/cloud debris from overnight activity) and steep mid-level lapse rates to yield strong buoyancy (e.g., upwards of 4000 J/kg of MLCAPE). Although directional shear will not be impressive in most locations, 30-40 kt of mid-level flow will be sufficient for a mixture of supercells and bowing clusters, capable of damaging winds and large hail through the afternoon and evening. The most likely area for robust instability overlapping organized convection (given focused warm advection / 850mb confluence) appears to exist near the mid Missouri Valley, and an enhanced risk has been introduced here, primarily for damaging winds. Farther west, a moist upslope regime behind the front should yield isolated to widely scattered convection over eastern Colorado and

sections.title: Upstate New York into northern New England
sections.text: Behind an initial impulse early in the day, an EML plume is expected to advance across the region later in the day into the early overnight. Additionally, a low-amplitude shortwave trough will likely yield isolated/widely scattered thunderstorms moving southeast from Ontario/Quebec during the evening. Near/south of a residual outflow/front, at least moderate levels of instability are expected, given surface dew points in the upper 60s/lower 70s. Ample mid-level flow and some veering with height should encourage at least isolated supercells/bowing clusters, with an attendant threat of damaging winds, large hail, and perhaps a tornado. ..Picca/Squitieri/Gleason.. 06/30/2018

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected from the central Plains to the Upper Midwest this afternoon and evening. Isolated to widely scattered severe storms will also be possible across parts of northern New York and northern New England.

sections.title: Eastern Nebraska/northern Kansas to Wisconsin/Michigan
sections.text: Located over the northern High Plains early today, a semi-potent upper trough by early summer standards will approach the region late today and especially tonight. A fairly complex evolution is expected today, owing to outflow boundaries from overnight convection, residual cloud cover, and multiple decaying MCVs, which could potentially be very subtle factors for convective initiation later today for areas such as eastern Nebraska/northeast Kansas. Regardless, the outflow reinforced boundary will extend northeastward from northern Kansas into east-central Nebraska toward the Upper Mississippi River Valley. Near/east of the front, dewpoints in the 70s F will combine with pockets of insolation (influenced by convective/cloud debris from overnight activity) and steep mid-level lapse rates to yield locally strong buoyancy (e.g., upwards of 4000 J/kg of MLCAPE). Deep-layer/low-level shear will be maximized in the immediate vicinity of the front, with deep-layer winds and mid-level capping generally weakening/increasing, respectively, to the east of the frontal boundary. The overall environment will support a mixture of supercells and bowing clusters, capable of large hail, damaging wind

sections.title: Front Range/Central High Plains
sections.text: Farther west, a moist post-frontal upslope regime should yield isolated to widely scattered convection over southeast Wyoming and eastern Colorado this afternoon and evening. Surface dew points in the 50s, some heating, and steep lapse rates aloft should yield moderate buoyancy, such that isolated supercells should develop within a highly sheared environment (40+ effective shear accentuated by long/strong hodographs above the boundary layer). These cells will be capable of large hail, possibly a brief tornado, along with locally damaging winds as they progress east/southeast from the Front Range vicinity toward the High Plains. Given the potential that scattered storms will move into the region this evening with some hail/wind risk, additional parts of western Nebraska and/or western Kansas could warrant a Slight Risk upgrade today provided greater certainty regarding post-frontal buoyancy.

sections.title: Upstate New York into northern New England
sections.text: Behind a weakening mid-level wave early today, an elevated mixed layer will continue to advect east/northeastward toward the region through tonight. A 7.3 C/km 700-500 mb lapse rate was noted with this morning's 12Z observed raob from Buffalo, NY while the 12Z Detroit sounding featured 8.8 C/km. The main potential for strong to severe thunderstorms should exist from mid/late afternoon through tonight. Multiple thunderstorm clusters and possible convectively related impulses/MCVs are noted across northern Ontario early today. It is likely that ascent related to these features, as they cross the northern periphery of the Mid-Atlantic States centered upper ridge, will spread toward upstate New York and northern New England late today through tonight. Moderate levels of instability are expected across the region, given surface dew points in the upper 60s/lower 70s and steepening lapse rates aloft. Ample mid-level flow and some veering with height would support bowing clusters and possibly some supercells, with an attendant threat of damaging winds, large hail, and perhaps a tornado as storms generally spread southeastward. ..Guyer/Peters.. 06/30/2018

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected from the central Plains to the Upper Midwest this afternoon and evening, as well as across parts of northern New York and northern New England.

sections.title: NY/New England
sections.text: Fast west-northwesterly flow aloft extends across Ontario/Quebec into the northeast states today, with the core of 500mb flow exceeding 60 knots. Water vapor imagery shows multiple subtle embedded shortwave troughs within the flow that will track into NY/New England later today, posing a risk of severe storms. The scenario with highest potential is for fast-moving cluster(s) of storms currently north/northwest of Georgian Bay to track eastward into parts of NY/VT/NE/ME this afternoon and early evening. Forecast soundings in this region show fast, deep westerly flow and moderate CAPE values. A severe bowing complex is possible, capable of rather widespread strong/damaging wind gusts. Therefore, have upgraded to ENH risk for this region.

sections.title: MN/IA/WI
sections.text: A weak convectively-induced mid level shortwave trough is lifting northeastward across eastern NE/SD. Strong heating and a very moist boundary layer ahead of this feature will yield strong afternoon instability and the development of scattered thunderstorms. The activity should spread northeastward across much of IA and southern MN into WI through the evening. Multicell to occasional supercell storm structures are expected, with damaging winds and hail the main threats.

sections.title: NE/KS/IA
sections.text: A stronger upper feature is currently tracking eastward across western WY. Lift ahead of this system will promote thunderstorm development over eastern WY and northeast CO by mid afternoon. Large hail will be possible in the strongest cells. These storms are expected congeal into a linear MCS through the early evening and track across NE and northern KS, and eventually into western IA. Given the consistent signal of models and observational trends, have extended the ENH risk farther west into central NE. ..Hart/Bentley.. 06/30/2018

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe thunderstorms are expected from the central Plains to the Upper Midwest this afternoon and evening, as well as across parts of northern New York and northern New England.

sections.title: 20Z Update
sections.text: ...West/Central OK...South-Central KS... Remnant MCV moving northeastward into far northwest TX is contributing to increased forcing for ascent as well as locally enhanced low to mid-level winds. Thunderstorms ahead of this system have produced severe wind gusts across far southwest OK and the downstream airmass is warm, moist, and very unstable, suggesting the potential for additional strong winds (and possibly isolated hail) will persist throughout the afternoon. As a result, 15% wind probabilities were introduced ahead of this MCS from west/central OK to south-central KS.

sections.title: Southwest NE...Northwest KS
sections.text: Temperature gradient along the northern periphery of the surface low continues to tighten as cloudiness from the western KS/NE border impedes heating. Resulting instability gradient may provide a favored path for the potential MCS coming out of northeast CO/southern NE Panhandle. This potential is confirmed by recently high-resolution guidance. In deference to this potential threat, 30% wind probability was extended a bit southwestward into more of southwest NE and northwest KS.

sections.title: Elsewhere
sections.text: Forecast outlined in the previous outlook remains valid. Short-term threat across eastern Nebraska, Iowa, and Southern Minnesota was addressed by MCD 952 and Severe Thunderstorm Watch 245. Short-term threat across northeast Colorado, southeast Wyoming, and western Nebraska was addressed MCD 954. ..Mosier.. 06/30/2018 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1112 AM CDT Sat Jun 30 2018/

outlooks.summary: Isolated to widely scattered severe thunderstorms are forecast mainly this evening from the central Great Plains to the Upper Great Lakes, as well as parts of northern New England.

sections.title: Central Great Plains to the Upper Great Lakes
sections.text: Several strong to severe thunderstorm clusters ongoing this evening are associated with several mid-level disturbances (both of convective origin and synoptic forcing) across the central Great Plains. A myriad of convective outflow has acted to partially overturn the airmass but corridors of 60s-70s degrees F dewpoints sampled by the 00Z Omaha RAOB suggest pockets of strong buoyancy remain. As a mid-level shortwave trough moves from the central High Plains this evening to eastern NE during the overnight, an eastward progression of a forced convective line will likely move east across the northern half of KS and NE. Severe gusts with localized wind damage will become the dominant severe risk by late evening. In the short term, cellular storms will be capable of a hail risk before updraft intensity gradually lessens with diurnal cooling. Farther east, several bands of thunderstorms will move across the IA/WI corridor where a plume of steep 700-500 lapse rates are located (refer to the 00Z Green Bay RAOB 7.7 degrees C/km). Multicells capable of isolated wind damage are the primary concern this evening before storms gradually weaken later this evening.

sections.title: New England
sections.text: The lack of convective initiation prior to dusk lends uncertainty whether storms will develop this evening across northern New England. Will maintain 15% wind probabilities yielding a Category 2 (Slight) risk for the possibility for storms to develop and intensify later this evening into the overnight. ..Smith.. 07/01/2018

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe threat will continue developing across northwest Iowa over the couple of hours. The threat is expected to also increase across southern Minnesota and in eastern Nebraska. Initially, wind damage and isolated large hail will be the primary threats. However, a tornado threat will also be possible as cells mature later this afternoon. Weather watch issuance will likely be needed across the region.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The latest surface analysis shows a cold front moving southeastward across southern Minnesota, northwest Iowa and eastern Nebraska. A moist airmass is in place near to the southeast of the front with surface dewpoints mostly in the mid to upper 70s F. This is resulting in moderate to strong instability (MLCAPE 2000 to 3000 J/kg) across the mid Missouri and upper Mississippi Valley. In addition, the northwestern edge of the warm sector is overlapped with moderate deep-layer shear. Forecast soundings at Omaha this afternoon have 0-6 km shear in the 45 to 50 kt range suggesting the environment will support supercells. The instability combined with steep lapse rates will make isolated large hail possible with supercells. As a weak capping inversion weakens and low-level lapse rates steepen further over the next few hours, a wind damage threat will be possible with short multicell line segments. Low-level shear is also forecast to increase during the late afternoon suggesting a tornado threat may develop as well.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A developing cluster of storms in northern Oklahoma will likely strengthen this afternoon as it moves into Oklahoma. These storms may produce some large hail and damaging winds as the storms move northeast this afternoon and into the evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of storms has started to develop in northern Texas ahead of a weak MCV. As the boundary layer destabilizes further across Oklahoma this afternoon, these storms will likely continue to strengthen. Deep-layer shear is weak across much of the Southern Plains, however the VWP from FDR and DYX is sampling an area of enhanced mid-level flow (35 to 40 knots around 5 km) associated with this MCV. Therefore, this combination of strong to very strong instability across Oklahoma combined with the locally enhanced shear associated with the MCV will provide an environment supportive of one or more multicell clusters. The primary threat from these storms will be large hail and damaging winds. No watch is expected ahead of the current convection, however a watch may be needed later this afternoon if this convection grows upscale and becomes a more widespread threat.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Storms will gradually increase in intensity through the afternoon. Large hail will be the primary threat initially with a greater wind damage threat through time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Storms have started to form on the front range of the Rockies this afternoon. While instability has been somewhat limited across most of southeast Wyoming and northern Colorado due to morning cloud cover, instability is sufficient (500 to 1000 J/kg MUCAPE) for strong updrafts. Unseasonably strong mid-level flow (50 to 60 knots per CYS VWP) combined with low-level easterly flow, provides a very favorable shear environment for organized storms. Initially, storms may struggle to intensify due to limited instability, but continued cloud breaks and low-level moist upslope flow will aid in destabilization and lead to an increasing severe weather threat through the afternoon. Steep mid-level lapse rates per DNR 12Z sounding will support large hail as the primary threat initially. The threat is expected to evolve into a greater wind threat through time as storm coverage increases and storms are expected to congeal into a linear MCS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe threat appears likely to continue to develop across parts of south and central Nebraska over the next couple of hours. Large hail and isolated wind damage will be possible. WW issuance will likely be issued for parts of southern and central Nebraska.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The latest surface analysis shows a 1004 mb low over southwest Kansas with a front extending northeastward from the low across southeastern Nebraska into western Iowa. Strong thunderstorms have initiated over the last hour to the north of the front across southern Nebraska. The airmass north of the front is moderately unstable with MLCAPE values estimated by the RAP in the 1500 to 3000 J/kg range. In addition, the Hastings WSR-88D VWP has 0-6 km shear values in the 45 to 50 kt range suggesting that organized convection will be likely. The wind profile should continue to support supercells and large hail will be possible with the stronger updrafts. Wind damage may also occur with supercells and short line segments. An isolated tornado threat can also not be ruled out as well mainly with cells that can remain discrete.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe storms in southwest Oklahoma are expected to continue northeast through the afternoon with primarily a damaging wind threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The cluster of storms in southwest Oklahoma has a history of producing 60 to 70 mph winds so far along its path. Considering the thermodynamic environment ahead of this cluster (3500+ J/kg MLCAPE) this cluster will likely continue to grow upscale as it moves northeast. While 0 to 6 shear is relatively weak (25 knots on the 18Z LMN sounding), it has proven sufficient for multicell organization of ongoing convection. Given the large buoyancy, large hail will continue to be a threat, however, damaging winds will be the primary threat from these storms.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe threat is expected to increase across WW 245 over the next couple of hours. Large hail, wind damage and perhaps a tornado or two may occur with the more intense cells.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The latest surface analysis continues to show a cold front moving through the southeast Minnesota and northern Iowa. The RAP is analyzing a sharp gradient of instability along the front with MLCAPE values to the southeast of the front estimated to be in the 2500 to 3500 J/kg range. The instability is being enhanced by a very moist boundary layer with surface dewpoints in the mid to upper 70s F. This combined with 0-6 km shear in the 45 to 50 kt range evident on the Omaha WSR-88D VWP will support severe storms. Cells that remain discrete may form into supercells and be associated with isolated large hail. The storms that organize into short line segments may have wind damage as the favored threat. As a low-level jet increases across the mid Missouri Valley late this afternoon into early evening, an isolated tornado threat will also be possible with the more dominant supercells. The severe threat is expected to gradually increase in coverage as more thunderstorms initiate along the front over the next few hours.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: One or more rounds of severe weather expected this evening. Damaging winds will be the primary threat, however, large hail is also possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Considerable uncertainty remains as to the timing of the greatest threat from storms this evening. A storm has now formed east of Ottawa where temperatures have risen into the upper 80s with dewpoints in the low 70s. The airmass ahead of these storms continues to destabilize this afternoon with the dewpoint in Burlington, Vermont rising from 62F to 68F in the last few hours. Continued advection of this moist low-level airmass will destabilize areas in northern New Hampshire and western Maine over the next few hours. Given the high theta-e airmass in the area combined with effective shear of 35 to 40 knots per the latest RAP mesoanalysis, expect any strong storms which develop to continue eastward. The greatest uncertainty involves the evolution of this activity. While most model guidance has been consistent with a bowing segment across this area later this evening, there have been varying solutions regarding the the intensity of earlier convection. If the current storm east of Ottawa strengthens or if additional development grows southeastward, a watch may be needed soon, however the primary concern remains with the threat of a bowing segment later this evening evolving from expected development in eastern Ontario.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A new Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be issued shortly to cover an increasing threat for damaging winds and isolated large hail across the region.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite depict deepening convection from parts of northern/central Wisconsin into the Upper Peninsula of Michigan. Additionally, a maturing convective system is slowly developing eastward across Watch 245. With rich boundary-layer moisture (e.g., surface dew points in the 70s) and steep mid-level lapse rates in place, strong MLCAPE (on the order of 3000-4000 J/kg) and modest deep-layer shear will support further cluster/multicell modes capable of damaging downburst winds and perhaps a few severe hail reports. To cover the threat, a watch will likely be issued shortly.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Developing storms will pose a risk of damaging winds and large hail. A watch may be needed if convective trends warrant.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A very evident MCV is lifting north/northeast towards the Kansas/Nebraska border this afternoon. Focused ascent ahead of and on the eastern flank of this circulation is assisting new convective development from the MCV to the KC Metro late this afternoon. Regional VWP data are not sampling much directional shear, but strong buoyancy combined with enhanced southwesterly flow aloft (around 35-45 kt at 6 km) will likely support damaging downburst winds and isolated large hail with cluster/multicellular modes. Convective coverage/organization may warrant new watch issuance.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Damaging winds will be possible with the strongest storms this evening. The overall organization of the threat should be limited, though, and a watch is not expected at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite depicts an MCV lifting northeast across the Edwards Plateau this afternoon, with some increase in convection noted in its vicinity. Additionally, to its east/northeast, a maturing cumulus field suggests convection will further increase in coverage into the early evening. SJT VWP and forecast soundings indicate little deep-layer shear. However, adequate buoyancy (MLCAPE around 1500-2000 J/kg) overlying a well-mixed/hot boundary layer will promote efficient evaporation in heavy precipitation cores. In turn, thunderstorm clusters may produce a few areas of damaging downburst winds through mid evening. A watch is not currently anticipated, however, owing to a lack of organization from weak tropospheric winds.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated severe threat continues across Severe Thunderstorm Watch 0246, with a WW issuance possible farther to the southeast. Large hail and isolated damaging wind gusts will be the main threats.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Isolated storms are ongoing from the Nebraska Panhandle to central Colorado, just east of the Rocky Mountains. As a 500 mb vort-max across south central Wyoming continues to move eastward, large scale lift may assist in initiating additional storms across Severe Thunderstorm Watch 0246 and perhaps points east (as indicated by recent CAM guidance). While buoyancy is rather modest immediately along the Colorado Front-range, 1500-2000 J/kg MLCAPE (driven by 7.5+ C/km mid-level lapse rates and 60+ F dewpoints) and 50+ knot effective bulk shear is present from far northeast Colorado into southwest Nebraska and northwest Kansas. This suggests favorable conditions for organized updrafts capable of at least isolated large hail and damaging wind gusts are in place. Multiple surface boundaries are present just to the southeast of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 0246 and storms may initiate along these boundaries in the next few hours. As such, convective trends will be monitored for potential eastward issuance of a new WW.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat will continue to transition towards primarily damaging winds across Watch 247, as well as Watches 245 and 250, this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Two distinct regimes of severe convection are ongoing across Watch 247 early this evening -- one with a linear system departing the Nebraska Panhandle and another with supercell clusters over southern Nebraska. The linear system is accelerating east into an area of modest surface-based buoyancy and some inhibition, as suggested by a 19Z LBF sounding. However, large-scale ascent associated with a sharp shortwave trough, a building cold pool behind the line, and favorable storm-relative flow may maintain the line as it pushes east. This evolution would favor a corridor of damaging winds over central Nebraska. Farther east, warm advection focused near the composite front/outflow is supporting a mixture of supercells and multicells. Increasing storm coverage and merging cold pools will likely favor an increasing wind threat here as well, possibly in the form of a small-scale convective system that accelerates east towards the Missouri River. Prior to this evolution, some tornado/hail threat will continue with any discrete cells, given favorable directional shear. ..Picca.. 06/30/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Primarily wind damage threat will continue with linear complex moving northeast. Greatest threat for severe gusts will be along the north-northeast portions of the line. A northeastward extension of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 0248 may be possible before expiration.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A linear complex has surged northeast across central Oklahoma, with marginally severe wind gusts observed within the last few hours. The latest observed gusts have mainly been constricted to northern portions of the line, where convection propagating northeastward parallel to stronger mid-level flow has allowed for cells to move in tandem with the cold pool. Large buoyancy (3000+ J/kg MLCAPE) resides out ahead of the north-northeast portions of the line, suggesting that at least isolated severe wind gusts will remain possible with the stronger cores for the next few hours. Convective trends are also being monitored just east of the bounds of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 0248, where at least modest instability is present. If organized convection persists towards this area, a localized WW extension may be necessary and convective trends will continue to be monitored.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Very isolated severe threat possible over the next few hours. Marginally severe hail and gusty winds would be the primary threats. Sparse and marginal nature of potential severe threat suggests a WW issuance is not likely at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An unstable airmass (with up to 2500 J/kg MLCAPE) and a moderately sheared environment (30+ knots effective bulk shear and 100-150 m2/s2 0-3km SRH) is present across the discussion area. So far, storms have been slow to initiate across the area, with large scale ascent associated with a 500mb vort-max remaining to the north of the region. Still, a well-mixed boundary layer is in place and a LLJ will be intensifying over the area shortly. As such, a slight uptick in convection is possible (also noted by recent CAM guidance). Given the modest ambient environment, any storms that form may produce mainly isolated, marginally severe hail/wind gusts. A WW issuance is not anticipated at this time.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Some damaging wind threat will persist to the east of Watch 245. Coverage of the threat may be too localized for new watch issuance, but trends will be monitored.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: At the intersection of two outflow boundaries near Tama Co, IA, a cluster of strong/severe convection has organized. This cluster may propagate east/southeastward along the outflow extending towards the Mississippi River, as convergence forces new cell development. Although tropospheric flow weakens with eastward extent, rich boundary-layer moisture and steep mid-level lapse rates may maintain a damaging wind threat with this cluster. Sufficient upscale growth and/or bowing could require new watch issuance. ..Picca.. 07/01/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Pockets of damaging wind potential remain, but the severe threat should continue to wane into the early overnight.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several convective regimes are ongoing across Watch 249 and northern parts of Watch 245 this evening. Over southern Wisconsin, the interaction of southeastward-moving outflow and a decaying HCR has promoted a small cluster of strong to briefly severe storms. Damaging winds are the primary threat here, but cells should weaken as outflow moves farther southeast and undercuts them. A secondary convective system is crossing the Mississippi River at present, but is encountering convectively processed air in the wake of a prior system. As such, a further downturn in intensity is anticipated. Lastly, clusters of strong/severe thunderstorms are ongoing over the U.P. of Michigan. Storms will continue to propagate along outflow boundaries, with pockets of residual steep lapse rates yielding a few updrafts strong enough for cells to briefly become capable of severe gusts. However, continued overturning will gradually reduce the threat here as well. ..Picca.. 07/01/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat continues across WW 0251. Damaging wind gusts are likely to be the predominant threat, though a brief tornado or two cannot be ruled out.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An outflow dominant supercell cluster in Yuma/Kit Carson counties Colorado is moving into Cheyenne/Sherman Counties in Kansas, with an additional supercell ongoing in Graham County, Kansas. These storms are progressing in an ambient environment characterized by 1500+ J/kg and 200+ m2/s2 SRH (owing to respectable low-level directional shear and a developing nocturnal LLJ). As the LLJ continues to increase in strength, enhanced convergence along the jet terminus may assist ongoing storms into growing upscale. As such, damaging winds will be possible with these storms before they become increasingly elevated due to a nocturnally cooled, stabilizing boundary layer. Any storm that can anchor to one of the outflow boundaries present across Severe Thunderstorm Watch 0251 may produce an isolated, brief tornado or two before becoming elevated later this evening.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Some damaging wind potential continues across the region, but the overall severe threat should further diminish this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Several clusters of strong to occasionally severe convection are ongoing across the region. The two most likely areas of severe/damaging wind potential exist ahead of a narrow, strongly forced line over central Nebraska and a residual reservoir of buoyancy between convective clusters over northeast Kansas. Through the evening, however, further expansion of WAA-aided convection and mergers of ongoing storms will result in significant overturning. Combined with nocturnal cooling, the severe threat should wane further. Of note, Watch 245 will be allowed to expire at 02Z. ..Picca.. 07/01/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated storms may move across the discussion area over the next few hours. Storms that can mature may produce isolated, marginally severe hail/wind gusts.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Buoyancy is decreasing across northern New England and the boundary layer is beginning to stabilize. Nonetheless, large scale ascent is glancing the area and sparse convection has initiated within the last hour. Deep-layer and low-level speed/directional shear highly favor updraft organization for any storms that may sustain themselves in the next few hours. Given the waning instability and increasing inhibition, marginally severe hail/damaging winds will likely be the primary threats with these storms. Given low confidence in greater storm coverage, a WW issuance may not be needed at this time, though convective trends will continue to be monitored.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: While there is a residual threat for a few damaging gusts, storms should weaken over the next few hours, reducing the severe threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A small line of strong/severe storms is moving east/southeast around 40-45 kt this evening. Despite increasing convective inhibition with eastward extent, strong forced ascent along the cold pool is sustaining robust convection within the line, and damaging/severe gusts have occurred intermittently with the line. Still, stable air with eastward extent, as well as weaker storm-relative inflow, should lead to a downward intensity trend over then next several hours. While a localized severe threat may continue through about 06Z, new watch issuance is not expected. ..Picca.. 07/01/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong/damaging wind gusts will pose a severe-weather threat across southeast into east-central Nebraska through 1-2 AM CDT, and could move into adjacent extreme west-central Iowa by 2 AM CDT, in vicinity of the Omaha and Council Bluffs areas. Limited spatial extent should preclude the need for a watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Trends in mosaic radar imagery during the early overnight indicated some acceleration of a forward-propagating line of storms moving into southeast and east-central NE at 0530Z, with the line extending from near KOLU to the NE/KS border at approximately 30 NNE KCNK. The air mass immediately downstream has undergone some destabilization during the last 1-2 hours with rising surface temperatures a degree or two. The passage of this line of storms at the Hastings NWS radar showed a well-defined strong rear inflow jet (50+ kt at 1-2 km agl). This jet combined with a 30-40 kt southwesterly low-level jet nosing into eastern NE/western IA will sustain modest instability and a favorable environment for continued fast storm motion with this line of storms during the next 2-3 hours. The greatest severe-weather threat should be into the OMA/Council Bluffs area, as this portion of the line of storms has recently accelerated to 45-50 kt, and is tending to favor the easterly low-level wind component near a surface boundary.
